source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.
prompt:
You are assisting with a scholarly experiment in structural literary analysis.

TASK: Write an ORIGINAL short prose passage in English, set in the target scenario below. It must be
a HOMEOSYNTACTIC transposition of a hidden source: hold the source's syntactic form at the level
specified below while inventing entirely new words and moving the content into the target
scenario. It is NOT a paraphrase or a translation.

FORM TARGET (hold this). Reproduce, period by period, the CLAUSE ARCHITECTURE below --- the same inventory and nesting of clauses (main / relative / adverbial / complement / coordinate, to the stated depth). The WORD ORDER and the words themselves are entirely yours; only the clause skeleton is fixed.
Reproduce it for all 10 periods, in this order:
Period 1 (~8 words) clause architecture: 1 main clause; subordination nested up to depth 0.
Period 2 (~29 words) clause architecture: 1 main clause; 1 open complement (infinitive); 1 adverbial clause; subordination nested up to depth 1.
Period 3 (~3 words) clause architecture: 1 main clause; subordination nested up to depth 0.
Period 4 (~15 words) clause architecture: 1 main clause; 1 relative/adnominal clause; subordination nested up to depth 1.
Period 5 (~11 words) clause architecture: 1 main clause; 1 adverbial clause; 1 relative/adnominal clause; subordination nested up to depth 2.
Period 6 (~9 words) clause architecture: 1 main clause; 1 relative/adnominal clause; 1 open complement (infinitive); subordination nested up to depth 2.
Period 7 (~12 words) clause architecture: 1 adverbial clause; 1 main clause; subordination nested up to depth 1.
Period 8 (~18 words) clause architecture: 1 main clause; subordination nested up to depth 0.
Period 9 (~19 words) clause architecture: 2 relative/adnominal clause; 1 main clause; 1 finite complement clause; 1 open complement (infinitive); subordination nested up to depth 4.
Period 10 (~9 words) clause architecture: 1 main clause; 1 finite complement clause; subordination nested up to depth 1.

TARGET SCENARIO --- render the content here (in your own words):
  - a supermarket checkout line at a busy hour
  - the conveyor belt, the barcode scanner, the bagging area, the card reader
  - the cashier and a shopper; a cart, a divider bar, a receipt
  - another shopper crowding from behind; a small friction over space in the queue
  - the register of retail routine: beeps, the total announced, loyalty-card prompts

REQUIREMENTS --- both hold together:
1. CLAUSE ARCHITECTURE PRESERVED --- the same clause inventory and nesting depth per period, in any word order and words you choose.
2. COHERENT --- one continuous, fully sensible passage in the target scenario; new lexicon,
   no trace of any source content.

Write modern, natural English. Produce the 10 periods in order as continuous prose --- no
numbering, no headings. Output ONLY the passage: no preamble, no self-audit.

gens.text:
In the thronged aisle, where the beeps hummed incessantly, she stood behind a divider bar, cart clutched tight. Her items slid by on the conveyor belt, barcode whirring under vigilant scanner eyes. The cashier announced the total with brisk efficiency, while loyalty-card prompts flashed above.

A rush stirred from her back, another shopper pushing in close. Fretfully, she adjusted the divider to preserve her space, a mere skirmish in the queue's ongoing battle. Her bag was nearly full; she felt the cart’s solid weight as she scanned each item, slotting them neatly into the plastic sacks.

The electronic hum intensified around her, and the cashier said, "Here’s your receipt." She took it, fumbling slightly but keeping to the register's rhythm. Behind her, someone else began their own transaction, another cycle in the supermarket's endless loop of goods and service.

In the bustling queue, a cart hummed on the belt. The scanner purred softly, its beeps steady. Behind, another shopper lingered, almost bumping against the divider bar. The cashier, with practiced ease, scooped up items into a bag. "Total's twenty-three," she announced. "Loyalty-card swipe next."

Her eyes flickered toward the encroacher. "Excuse me, please step back," she said, voice polite but firm.

At the other end, the shopper selected her loyalty card from the stack, inserted it into the reader, and waited. The screen lit with a message, “Welcome Back! Points earned.” She glanced at her watch, then at the beeping register. Her cart, now mostly bagged, shifted slightly on the belt.

Behind her, the crowd inched forward. "Must you stay there?" the cashier murmured, gesturing toward the space.

The shopper took a step back, and the conveyor belt resumed its rhythm. Beeps filled the air once more as each item slid through. The total was announced again: twenty-three dollars. She collected her receipt and exited the line with practiced speed, leaving the queue to steady itself behind her.

In the pulse of the bustling line, items slid across the belt, their barcodes scanned with a swift whoosh. The cashier tapped away on her interface, adding each item to the bagging area with practiced efficiency. The shopper's cart moved forward, the divider bar sliding smoothly over it. Behind them, another customer edged closer, murmuring an apology as she pushed past. The air was thick with tension, whispers of a small friction in the queue.

The beeps of items being scanned cut through the hum of background chatter. "Total will be..." the cashier announced, her voice clear and brisk. As if summoned, the loyalty-card prompt flashed across the screen, beckoning for swiping.

A brief pause, then the next customer stepped into view, holding their card out eagerly. The screen changed, now displaying a new series of tasks: choose payment method, enter PIN. There was no time to hesitate; the line demanded movement forward.

The bagging area hummed with activity, each item placed thoughtfully, ensuring minimal space wastage. A subtle shift in position brought the receipt printer into view, its ribbon hissing softly as it produced a slip of paper detailing the purchase. The cashier's fingers moved quickly, sealing the bag and handing it over.

The line continued to flow, beeps and announcements mingling with ambient noise. Each step forward was deliberate, the rhythm of retail routine carrying all on board through the process.

In the bustling line, the conveyor's rhythmic hum set a pace. The shopper ahead, her cart held steady by the divider bar, swiped and scanned with hurried efficiency. Behind, another pushed forward, crowding near as if to speed up the process. The beeps of beeping items filled the air, each one marking a passing second. 

The cashier, eyeing the total on the screen, murmured it softly for the shopper's benefit. "Fifty-five dollars and forty-three cents," she said, reaching for the loyalty-card slot where the customer could insert it. Meanwhile, the bagger at work in the back area worked to wrap each item neatly.

Behind, the divider bar wavered slightly as one person stepped closer, nearly bumping shoulders with another. "Can you please step back?" the cashier politely requested, her tone a hint of impatience. 

The shopper reached for their card, pausing to check if it was in pocket. The register beeped each time they inserted and removed it, the small delay adding to the growing tension in the line. 

As the last item was bagged and placed into a plastic bag, the cashier said, "Is there anything else I can help you with?" The other shopper, their patience wearing thin, gently nudged forward once more.

The beeps resumed as the items were rung up again. A moment later, the customer’s card buzzed briefly before returning to its pocket. The receipt was handed over, and the bag held steady by the divider bar, as the final beep signaled the end of the transaction.

In the hum of a bustling checkout line, the conveyor belt whispered softly, scanning each item. Behind the cashier's screen, the bagger deftly placed groceries into bags as the customer picked up her receipt. Suddenly, a second shopper poked anxiously from behind, nearly touching the divider bar; she adjusted her cart to give space, but an almost imperceptible friction lingered.

The register beeped with the addition of each item, followed by the total: twenty-two dollars and seventy-five cents. A gentle prompt for swiping the loyalty card filled the air, repeated softly until finally acknowledged. The cashier smiled warmly as the customer placed her card on the reader; the screen lit up to confirm the purchase.

As the items slid into a bag, the bagger paused briefly to tuck a small jar of jam neatly in place. The first shopper reached for her receipt, scanning it with a contented glance before folding it carefully into her purse. Behind them, the second shopper moved forward, already considering what else might be needed from this trip to the supermarket.

The beep of each item repeated like a familiar rhythm: apples, milk, detergent, snacks. Each product added its own weight to the transaction, and with every beep, the customer’s expression shifted slightly, gauging satisfaction or hesitation.

Inside the bag, the items settled into their places—each one fitting just right. As the second shopper approached, the first customer took a step back, offering space without complaint; both had learned the register of retail routine: beeps, totals, and that momentary tension as the line thinned and thickened with each newcomer.

In the bustling line, the conveyor belt hummed softly, while the barcode scanner whirred and beeped, each pulse announcing the next item. Behind me, a cart loomed, heavy with groceries. The cashier’s light bar flashed, dividing us, marking my own space as finite. A shopper crept closer from behind, squeezing past the divider with an apologetic nudge, setting off a small tug at the space.

She tugged her receipt as I scanned, my fingers quick on the keys. The total announced, crisp and clear; it beeps of confirmation mingled with loyalty-card prompts, their electronic hums echoing in the narrow aisle. 

My gaze flickered to the shopper behind me, who had taken a seat, his cart at a slight angle, encroaching on my queue like a misplaced puzzle piece. He watched, his eyes lingering on the transactions, as though the sequence of items and prices bore some hidden significance.

Her bag was passed with practiced ease, each item slid into its designated spot. The belt snaked away, taking the cart with it, while I moved my basket to the side; a silent choreography of daily routine, punctuated by the constant beeping and occasional chatter.

The space between us seemed to stretch momentarily as she pulled out her loyalty card, swiping quickly through the scanner. Her transaction concluded swiftly, leaving no time for lingering. The line resumed its steady pace, each step forward a microcosm of retail efficiency.

Her receipt fluttered onto the conveyor belt, folding neatly into my hand. The last few seconds lingered in silence, the line shifting with fluidity. The next item arrived, setting off another cycle, another moment in the endless stream of everyday transactions.

In a bustling line, a cart hummed past the scanner; its contents lit up on the screen, where digits danced under a cashier's watchful eye. Nearby, another shopper pushed forward, barely able to squeeze through the divider bar. The conveyor belt snaked around the corner, while a bagger stood ready with fresh plastic. Beeps echoed softly as each item was counted; the total announced clearly before loyalty-card prompts flashed, urging savings. 

A small friction grew in the queue; the cashier's tone remained calm and professional. She tapped out instructions for the new arrival to join smoothly, ensuring no delays. As bags were handed out, the line flowed forward, a steady stream of purchases passing through the register like a silent ballet. The card reader clicked softly as transactions concluded, leaving behind the hum of everyday commerce.

In a bustling supermarket checkout line, the conveyor belt hummed softly, moving shopping carts with gentle insistence. Behind her, a cart divider jutted forward, separating her from the surging crowd. As she pushed items through the scanner, another shopper pressed into the queue, their bagged purchases almost bumping against hers. The beeps of the scanner cut through the background noise, announcing the cost of each item.

Faster now, moving things along faster. But then a quick, muttered request for a loyalty-card scan; she leaned forward to tap her card, her eyes scanning the receipt with growing impatience. The crowd grew thicker behind them, pushing the air around in little turbulent swirls. 

A shopper in front of her hurried, picking up speed at the last minute. Her cart moved through the gap just as another customer's approached, narrowly avoiding a collision. A quick glance over, and a sharp nod for thanks as she reached out to grab the divider bar, her grip firm but steady.

The beep of the scanner repeated, each item adding to the total amount. With every addition came a brief moment of hesitation; it felt like they had all been in this exact place at that very second before. The cashier's prompt to insert a card broke through their collective reverie.

In the long line at the busy supermarket, the conveyor belt hummed steadily, scanning barcodes and moving items to be bagged. Behind us, a person pushed their cart close, nearly touching mine with the divider bar; I felt their slight pressure but did not move. The cashier spoke clearly, "Beep, beep," each item's price added to our total. My loyalty card was read too, prompting discounts for regular shoppers.

A receipt appeared and fluttered out from the slot, settling on top of my groceries. Another shopper moved forward, trying to squeeze in but stopped just shy of the divider, maintaining a polite distance. The conveyor belt slowed slightly as more items were scanned, then resumed its steady pace. "Your total is sixty dollars," the cashier announced, and I reached for my wallet, feeling the familiar weight of coins and notes.

The bagger's hands moved swiftly behind the counter, filling each plastic bag with an efficiency born from many years of retail routine. The beeps grew louder as more items were scanned, each one contributing to our final total. A small friction arose over who should step back; I gently nudged forward, allowing room for the next customer without causing a full-blown altercation.

A new item beeped into existence on the conveyor belt, and its price was added. "Here's your receipt," the cashier said with a smile as she handed it to me along with my bag of groceries. The line began to move again, and I followed behind, ready for the next round of transactions.

In the rush of the early evening, a conveyor belt hummed quietly while goods slid towards the barcode scanner like eager customers. A shopper, holding a cart full of groceries, stood ready behind a divider bar, awaiting her turn at the register. As she waited, the receipt printer began to whirr gently into life.

Behind her, another shopper, carrying a smaller but equally filled bag, tried to squeeze closer. The edge of the cart nudged slightly against the previous barrier, creating an accidental pause in the flow of the line. "Sorry," the first shopper murmured.

The cashier, focused on the task at hand, began by swiping each item past the scanner. Beeps echoed softly, announcing each addition to the total. As she completed one transaction, loyalty-card prompts flashed up—discounts for regular customers, a reminder of savings in store. 

Meanwhile, the items moved steadily from the conveyor belt to be bagged. Once her own items were processed, the first shopper reached out to slide them into bags laid at her feet. Her movements were practiced and efficient.

In that moment, as the second shopper pushed forward impatiently, a brief friction arose in the orderly queue. The cashier, still focused on the next customer, acknowledged the impatience with a calm nod towards the end of the line. Beeps continued to announce each purchase as the scanner checked out more items.

The first shopper’s receipt was handed over; she took it and stepped forward, her bag already half-filled. Behind her, the second shopper began to bag their own groceries, waiting for the next turn in the continuous cycle of the supermarket checkout.
